lots.guide_summary: Two sold hammers at Gowans for plain broad axes ($85 Apr 2026, $120 Mar 2026), both rougher than this one; a mixed spanner lot with a Plumb broad axe made $180 (category only). No unsold or verified asking evidence survives. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD $85 / 1.22 = $69.67, round down to $65. Flip: likely resale about $100 hammer (midpoint of $85 and $120) through a Tasmanian room, less about 15% vendor commission = $85, no outbound postage (local pickup buyer) = $85 / 2.44 = $34.84, round down to $30. Inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification as a broad axe is clear, and there are 2 opened Gowans SOLD results, but the maker stamp is unreadable in the photos (cropped and enlarged, only a faint letter group visible) and the comparables have no descriptions, so the rules put this at Low.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all three ASKING entries. eBay itm/156951267909 (AU $213.50 Plumb): snippet only, eBay is closed to us, the researcher said the URL is for a Dunlap axe, and it was unclear if sold or asking. plusmodels.com E. Williams US $238.99: page returned 403 (Cloudflare) so not verifiable, and it is a maker-marked US axe, not comparable. ebay.de/itm/155318506712 goosewing bearded axes US $109-119: snippet only, eBay closed, different style. Armitage site search not run: the WebSearch budget for this session was used up.
lots.key_photo_findings: 5 photos. Offset handle in reddish hardwood (looks recent or refinished), shaped timber stop behind the eye, fitted timber blade guard. Head grey and pitted, edge bright from fresh grinding. A stamp in the middle of the face (photos 3 and 4) is worn; enlarged crop shows only a faint mark and letters, not readable. A pink paint or chalk mark near the eye. No obvious cracks seen.
lots.condition: Cleaned and sharpened working condition, light pitting, handle sound in photos and likely a replacement. Not untouched collector condition.
lots.question_for_armitage: Can you read the maker stamp on the face of the axe head (e.g. Kelly, Plumb, Gilpin, a Tasmanian or Sheffield maker)? Is the handle tight in the eye and is the head left or right bevelled?

lots.guide_summary: All sold, all Gowans hammers in AUD. Close evidence: single Wakefield Castrol tins $23 and $40 (Nov 2025), a 3-tin Castrol/BP lot $30 and a 2-tin lot $25 (Jul 2026). Category only: early Neptune HVI gallon tin $280, Golden Fleece and Neptune kerosene tins $240, mixed boxes $35 to $81. No unsold or asking evidence. lots.working: Keep: lowest close whole-lot SOLD $30 (3 tins incl Castrol) / 1.22 = $24.59, round down to $20 (the single Wakefield tin at $23 would give $18, so $20 is already generous). Flip: split resale from SOLD evidence, Wakefield tin about $30 (mid of $23 and $40) plus the other three as a lot about $30 = $60, less about 15% vendor commission = $51, no outbound postage (local) = $51 / 2.44 = $20.90, round down to $20. Inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: All four labels are read in the photo and several opened Gowans SOLD results with photos match the Wakefield tin, but no sale of this exact set or this Neptune trident design was found.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped 397516 CALTEX OIL TIN $10: Gowans photo shows a 20 litre Caltex Aqua Tec outboard oil drum, not a one-gallon Caltex RPM tin. Downgraded 410781 and 366129 from close to category guide (photos show drums/fuel cans and a modern 5 litre GTX2 tin). Armitage site search not run: WebSearch budget for this session was used up.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. Left to right: Wakefield Castrol XL Special? Motor Oil (green, worn, rust spots), Caltex RPM Motor Oil SAE (red and white, rust on edges), Neptune Lubricant trident tin with paper overlabel reading about 'Extol B SAE 30' (rust through white band), Castrol XL with Liquid Tungsten 20W-50 with royal warrant crest (rust along base). All caps appear present. No big dents visible from the front; backs and bases not shown.
lots.condition: Fair, used and rusty display tins; labels readable, surface rust on all four, worst on the Neptune and the base of the Castrol XL.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are the backs and bases of the four tins sound (no rust holes), are caps present, and are any still holding oil?

lots.guide_summary: All sold, all Gowans hammers in AUD, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026: single sets on skull $35 to $65 (typically $45), 2-set lots $55 to $90, a 3-set lot $80. No unsold or asking evidence survives. No 5-set lot found, so the value of this lot is inferred: about $80 to $150 hammer as one lot.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close multi-set SOLD (3 sets, $80) / 1.22 = $65.57, round down to $65; a 5-set lot should not make less than a 3-set lot. Flip: resell as five single sets at about $45 each (the most common single-set hammer) = $225, less about 15% vendor commission = $191, no outbound postage (local) = $191 / 2.44 = $78.28, round down to $75. Inbound freight $0. Flip depends on splitting into five lots.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification (no mark needed) and many opened Gowans SOLD results, one with a photo closely matching, but no lot of five sets, Gowans has no condition text, and the antler count per lot is partly visible only.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Manfred Schotten sportantiques.co.uk fallow antlers on shield: no price shown, a decorative shield-mounted dealer piece, not comparable. Armitage site search not run: WebSearch budget for this session was used up.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos. Five skull plates visible, each bleached white with nail holes for hanging. Two sets of dark brown palmate fallow antlers (one with a long sweeping beam), three paler, weathered multi-tine red deer type sets, one with chalky flaking. Hang tags on a couple. Tines look mostly complete but tips and back of plates are hard to see.
lots.condition: Weathered shed/wall display condition, plates clean, some antlers chalky or flaking, no mounts or shields.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are there five complete sets (both antlers attached to each plate) and any broken tines or loose antlers?
